stories.h: Clayface tops US box office; Theranos doc climbs
sum: DC's R-rated body-horror spin-off Clayface opened at No. 1 in North America with about $24m, earning an A- CinemaScore on a reported $44m budget. A24's three-hour Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything did something rare: its takings rose 25% in its second weekend as it expanded, adding $19.5m for $45.1m total, already among the biggest documentaries ever.

Laika's stop-motion fantasy Wildwood opened third with $11.8m, while Street Fighter fell 72% to fourth. Olivia Colman's Wicker debuted fifth. The overall weekend reached $94.9m, up nearly 22% on last year, with 2026 running 20% ahead year to date.
pts: Clayface: $24m domestic, A- CinemaScore
You Can See Everything up 25% in week two
US year-to-date $8.4bn, +20% vs 2025

stories.h: Clayface's $43m global start sparks Morbius talk
sum: Clayface's worldwide opening came to $43m: $24m in North America plus $19m overseas. Both figures landed under pre-release forecasts of $25–35m domestic and $20–25m international, and some analysts compared it to Sony's Morbius as a warning sign for DC.

ComicBookMovie argues the comparison is overstated. Relative to budget, Clayface's opening is roughly in line with Morbius, but its reviews and audience scores are far stronger. The site estimates the film needs around $80–100m worldwide to break even once marketing and theatre splits are counted.
pts: $43m global opening on $44m budget
Missed forecasts at home and abroad
Break-even estimated at $80–100m

stories.h: Clayface: gory, gritty, but predictable
stories.why: For horror fans curious about DC
sum: James Watkins directs this Batman-adjacent origin story, written by Mike Flanagan and Hossein Amini. Tom Rhys Harries plays a Hollywood actor on the brink of fame who is disfigured in a violent attack in Gotham and turns to a scientist's experimental treatment, with Naomi Ackie as the woman by his side.

Screen's Tim Grierson welcomes how modest, edgy and gruesome it is compared with typical superhero blockbusters, and praises the leads' warm chemistry. But he finds the monster story and love story don't fully mesh, the Hollywood satire thin, and the final act generic and easy to predict.
pts: R-rated body horror, 108 minutes
Strong leads, B-movie grit
Familiar beats sink the last act

stories.h: The Liberation: Carrie Coon's awards-calibre turn
stories.why: Prestige drama with a great lead
sum: Guy Nattiv's drama, inspired by his own grandmother, follows Rita, a woman in 1980s New Jersey whose outwardly settled life hides a heavy past. She is drawn into a group led by a younger, magnetic woman named Ricki, played by Lily James, with Tracy Letts, Odessa Young and Bella Ramsey in support.

Screen calls it expertly observed and singles out Coon's performance as a tour de force and likely awards contender. The film carefully shows both the pull of the group and the danger beneath it, before tightening into psychological-thriller territory in its last third. It premiered at Telluride and opens in the US in January via Bleecker Street.
pts: Coon tipped for awards season
Lily James ambiguous and compelling
US release January 2027

stories.h: Beautiful Pain: good intentions, shallow drama
sum: This Indonesian drama, in cinemas since 22 October, is Dmaz Brodjonegoro's feature debut, co-written with Hanung Bramantyo and Titien Wattimena. Raihaanun plays Niken, a wife enduring domestic abuse and infidelity who also faces harassment at work and tries to rebuild her life alone. CNN Indonesia notes it appears inspired by Nikita Mirzani's life.

The critic gives it 3 and praises its clear message about women resisting violence and patriarchy, plus strong work from Raihaanun, Siti Fauziah and Jajang C Noer. But the plot is simplistic, Baim Wong's abusive husband is underwritten, and it sometimes slides into soap-opera territory.
pts: Rated 3 by CNN Indonesia
Raihaanun and Siti Fauziah shine
Thin conflicts, soapy at times

stories.h: Miracle in Cell No. 7 director shoots Indonesian film Gasigogi
sum: Falcon Pictures has announced Gasigogi, directed by South Korea's Lee Hwan-kyung, who made the original Miracle in Cell No. 7. Vino G. Bastian, who starred in that film's Indonesian remake, plays Jiwa, a father willing to give up everything to save his son Juna, who has blood cancer.

Pevita Pearce and Faradina Mufti co-star, with Indro Warkop, Dea Panendra and Indra Jegel among the supporting cast. The title is the Korean name for a small fish whose male guards its eggs alone, a symbol of parental sacrifice. The film is still in production and has no release date yet.
pts: Falcon Pictures production, set in Indonesia
Vino G. Bastian, Pevita Pearce lead
No release date yet

stories.h: Tarantino previews Fincher's Cliff Booth film at AFI
sum: At AFI Fest in Los Angeles, Quentin Tarantino surprised a crowd by screening the first 17 minutes of The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, his script directed by David Fincher, with Brad Pitt back as the stuntman from Once Upon a Time in Hollywood. The footage won't be released publicly.

Set eight years after the first film, the opening reportedly finds Cliff out of stunt work and managing a Los Angeles revival cinema, before the story drifts into gangsters, blackmail and the movie business. Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Peter Weller appear. It plays in IMAX worldwide from 25 November, then streams on Netflix from 23 December.
pts: Fincher directs, Tarantino wrote
IMAX run from 25 November
On Netflix 23 December
stories.q: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth

stories.h: New Avengers: Doomsday spot reunites Cap and Thor
sum: Marvel released a new 30-second extended TV spot for Avengers: Doomsday, following a sneak peek the day before. It gives a longer look at Steve Rogers and Thor reuniting, plus an extended gag where Ant-Man struggles over which Captain America to address, now with U.S. Agent joining in.

The Russo brothers' film, out 18 December, unites the Avengers, X-Men and Fantastic Four against Doctor Doom, with a huge cast led by Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans and Chris Hemsworth. Test-screening reactions reportedly praise Doom, and a final trailer is expected before release.
pts: 30-second extended TV spot
Release date 18 December
Final trailer still to come

stories.h: Clio Barnard's Birmingham drama wins Rome Film Fest
sum: Clio Barnard's I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning took best film in the Rome Film Fest's Progressive Cinema competition, which wrapped on 24 October. The film follows a group of childhood friends nearing 30 who must face that their dreams haven't worked out; it previously won the audience award in Cannes' Directors' Fortnight.

Its star Anthony Boyle shared best actor. Tim Blake Nelson's Amanda Seyfried prison drama took the grand jury prize, Diego Luna's Ashes won best screenplay, and Victoria Luengo won best actress for Spanish heist film Saints. The festival sold over 82,000 tickets across 194 films.
pts: Best film: I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning
Anthony Boyle shares best actor
Diego Luna's Ashes wins screenplay
stories.q: I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning

stories.h: Nothing new from Beyoncé or Kendrick Lamar today
sum: No releases, tour dates, features or announcements in the last 24 hours.

stories.h: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders take My Chemical Romance to court
sum: My Chemical Romance are playing The Black Parade in full at the Hollywood Bowl for its 20th anniversary, and the staging includes a fictional regime storyline. During the show on October 22, dancers dressed like Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders did a routine during "Teenagers", then joined a staged shootout with the regime's soldiers during "Disenchanted".

The company that owns the Cheerleaders brand asked a court for a temporary restraining order and injunction. It says fans online mistook the dancers for the real squad and that the violent skit could harm its image. MCR ignored a cease-and-desist letter and repeated the bit at the second Bowl show.
pts: Filing seeks a restraining order and injunction
Band repeated the skit the next night anyway
Filed the same day the real Cheerleaders unionized
stories.q: My Chemical Romance The Black Parade

stories.h: Turnstile play to 60,000 at the Washington Monument for aid
stories.why: Rock's biggest crossover band right now
sum: Baltimore hardcore band Turnstile closed the latest leg of their Never Enough tour with a free benefit show at the Washington Monument on Saturday, drawing an estimated 60,000 people. Run with Human Concern International, it raised money for humanitarian relief in Palestine, Sudan and Lebanon, beating a $100,000 goal to pass $220,000 by Sunday.

Frontman Brendan Yates, nursing an injured ankle, called it a homecoming and led a 19-song, 75-minute set. The free show echoes Fugazi's 1990s gigs near the same spot. Turnstile won two Grammys this year, including Best Rock Album, and play Camp Flog Gnaw next month.
pts: Estimated 60,000 people, free entry
Over $220,000 raised, more than double the goal
Echoes Fugazi's free DC shows of the 1990s

stories.h: Sam Fender scraps premium standing tickets after fan backlash
stories.why: Indie-rock star taking on ticket pricing
sum: Fans complained about prices for Sam Fender's 2027 UK stadium tour, which included a front-standing tier costing about £131 at Wembley. Fender said he hadn't known about the split standing areas and that prices had climbed higher than he wanted. He has now dropped the premium tier, so every standing ticket has the same chance of reaching the front.

General standing is now £85 and seats run from £55 to £95, before fees. The tour starts with two shows at St James' Park in Newcastle in June, with Wunderhorse supporting. Fans who pre-order his upcoming fourth album get a pre-sale on October 28. General sale opens October 30.
pts: Front-standing tier dropped; standing now £85
Album pre-order pre-sale starts Oct 28
Wunderhorse support the stadium dates

stories.h: Stereogum's 5 best songs: Cloud Nothings go heavy
sum: Stereogum's weekly top five puts Cloud Nothings first with "Death Keeps Me Alive", a standout from a new album where metal sharpens the band's sound. Next is Bassvictim's "White Flag", a harsh lo-fi electroclash song about surrender that sounds more like a fight. Third is Hannah Frances's "Circadian Heart", a restless, shape-shifting song about chasing people you can't have that ends in release.

The last two are sadie's bright, bouncy "Little Things", which makes ordinary details feel magical, and Worldpeace DMT's "Ringtone", a catchy love song that is both elegant and cheesy. Indie and alt fans have a lot to add to their playlists here.
pts: No. 1: Cloud Nothings, "Death Keeps Me Alive"
Also: Bassvictim, Hannah Frances, sadie, Worldpeace DMT
Heavy on indie and alt-rock
stories.q: Cloud Nothings Death Keeps Me Alive

stories.h: Ugly's debut The South Facade is a prog-pop thrill
stories.why: Adventurous UK indie in your lane
sum: London band Ugly have built a following over about ten years. Their debut album leaves behind the Bloc Party-style indie of their early singles for progressive rock and jazz fusion. The Line of Best Fit compares them to Black Country, New Road: dense arrangements, intricate melodies and bright harmonies that stay catchy rather than tiring.

Highlights include the yacht-rock gloss of "Die Another Day", the piano-rock and Santana-style solo of "In Samphedoo", and "Gavement", which the review calls the peak. It places Ugly closer to eccentric British pop like XTC than to show-off prog. The verdict: one of 2026's most creative debuts.
pts: Prog and jazz-fusion turn from a London indie band
For fans of Black Country, New Road
Best track: "Gavement"

stories.h: Michael Kiwanuka's FUDGE drifts beautifully, sometimes too long
sum: Kiwanuka's new album was delayed almost a year by health problems. It is his first since 2012 made without producers Inflo and Danger Mouse, yet it keeps their dreamy, psychedelic looseness. The Line of Best Fit praises the floating opening stretch, including "Summer Clothes" and "Love In My Heart", plus the fuzzier guitars of "Stars".

The main complaint is length. At just over an hour, tracks like "You Sent Me Flying" and "Steve's Paradis" linger without going anywhere. Still, the review finds it moving that he lets himself wander after a hard stretch, calling the album often beautiful and sometimes strange. NME is warmer and reads it as a powerful portrait of fragility.
pts: First album since 2012 without Inflo and Danger Mouse
Standout tracks: "Summer Clothes" and "Stars"
Main complaint: over an hour long

stories.h: The Black Parade at 20: emo's arena-sized masterpiece
stories.why: Alt-rock classic, timely with MCR news
sum: For the album's 20th anniversary, Stereogum's Tom Breihan says he was wrong to brush off The Black Parade in 2006. He argues it is My Chemical Romance's masterpiece and the defining record of emo's arena era, the last time guitar rock truly dominated youth culture. The band went all in on a concept, costumes and a story mapped out before the songs were written.

He hears them reaching for Queen and the Smashing Pumpkins rather than their Warped Tour peers. He admits flaws like the "Mama" section and names "Teenagers" the best track. The album went quadruple platinum, and he says the stadium-sized reunion shows confirm its standing.
pts: Writer admits he underrated it in 2006
Best track, he says: "Teenagers"
Went 4x platinum; reunion shows play it in full
stories.q: My Chemical Romance The Black Parade

stories.h: Cabinet Couture: the Instagram tracking Indonesian officials' luxury
sum: An anonymous collective behind the Instagram account Cabinet Couture photographs Indonesian politicians and their families flaunting designer goods, identifies each item and reposts it with a price tag. It started days after the September 2025 protests sparked by the police killing of delivery rider Affan Kurniawan, gained almost 120,000 followers in a week and now has over 277,000.

Its original account was geo-blocked inside Indonesia by the communications ministry, so the team relaunched as season 2. Their core point is the gap between officials' declared wealth reports (LHKPN) and their visible lifestyles. Fans and luxury-industry insiders send tips, and the group links the work to the wider 17+8 reform demands.
pts: Started after the Sept 2025 Jakarta protests; 277k+ followers
First account blocked in Indonesia, now @cabinetcouture_season2
Compares LHKPN wealth reports with flexed designer buys

stories.h: Chappell Roan's laced leather top is from Eden Sherry
stories.why: Rock-edged look from an indie label
sum: When Chappell Roan guested on Charli xcx's tour, she wore a slashed black leather top studded with grommets and stitched together with laces. Stylist Hunter Clem commissioned it from Eden Sherry, a 2024 London College of Fashion graduate who made it in a single day from London deadstock leather. She calls the shape a cascade of falling belts.

Sherry was born in New Zealand and raised in Hong Kong, and she launched her label in 2025 after winning an award in Portugal. She credits Lady Gaga's Bad Romance era and McQueen as influences, and FKA twigs has worn one of her bag tops on a Rolling Stone cover. Her first live presentation is planned for next summer.
pts: Grommeted, lace-hemmed top made from deadstock leather
Label launched in 2025; FKA twigs is already a fan
First live show planned for summer 2027

stories.h: Sophia Wilson styles Dr. Martens as a former tomboy
sum: For Dr. Martens' With Bouncing Soles campaign, which also features Chloë Sevigny and Naomi Watanabe, photographer Sophia Wilson made a portrait series called The Joy of Girlhood. It centers on the brand's Crazy Horse leather line, which is built to weather with wear. The styling mixes grunge, vintage tailoring and preppy pieces, chosen to show off each sitter's personality.

Wilson calls herself a former tomboy whose first Docs were holographic. She says artists should make work from their own point of view instead of chasing trends. The project launched with a New York party on October 8, where she wore new 1461s.
pts: Crazy Horse leather is made to age and scuff
Mix of grunge, vintage tailoring and prep
Wilson wore 1461 shoes to the NYC launch

stories.h: TYAKASHA x KEEN mismatched green-and-blue slide
sum: Japanese label TYAKASHA reworked KEEN's Howser III slip-on so each foot is different: one is forest green and the other is icy Mediterranean blue. Both have nubby fleece-like uppers, warm brown trim, bright orange bungee laces and embroidered patches of the brand's mascots, Mr. Green and Oring.
It also has a chunky rubber sole and a plush brown lining. The slide released on October 21 for ¥12,650 (about US$80) through KEEN Japan's online store.
pts: Mismatched colors: green on one foot, blue on the other
Orange bungee laces and mascot embroidery
About US$80 on keenfootwear.jp

stories.h: Liberaiders turns the adidas Superstar into fuzzy blue
sum: Tokyo label Liberaiders swapped the adidas Superstar's smooth leather for long-haired blue material, with smoother blue panels on the eyestays and tongue. The shell toe, laces, sole and Three Stripes are creamy off-white, and the sidewall branding is gold.

An embroidered white origami crane, Liberaiders' emblem, sits on the tongue and appears again on the insoles and packaging. It comes in this one colorway only and was set to drop on October 24 through Japanese retailer SOULGOODS. The price was not yet confirmed.
pts: Shaggy blue upper on a classic shell toe
Origami crane embroidered on the tongue
One colorway only, sold at SOULGOODS

stories.h: Kiko Kostadinov x ASICS GEL-SJ33 in plum and green
sum: Kiko Kostadinov's ASICS GEL-SJ33 is back in two new colorways. Moonrock/Tatami Green has a taupe-to-grey mesh with teal and mint linework and pale blue stripes. Deep Plum/Fresh Grass has a violet base with black and purple lines, maroon accents and bright green branding.

The shoe is based on the 2010s GEL-Super J33 and adds a heel counter and a medial strap. It runs on GEL-Cumulus 16 tooling with FlyteFoam cushioning. Both pairs released on October 23 for US$170 at asics.com, following two coffee-toned pairs from this summer.
pts: Two colorways: grey/mint and plum/green
US$170 on asics.com
Based on the 2010s GEL-Super J33

stories.h: Burna Boy x On: a bright-red Cloudmonster
sum: Burna Boy's first sneakers with On are out now, tied to his No Giant Stands Alone campaign. The Cloudmonster BB is bright red all over, with darker red tonal branding. THE ROGER Clubhouse BB is an all-white tennis shoe with shaggy textured laces and two red stitch details on the heel.
A Cloudtilt Remix is also planned for the capsule, but it hasn't been shown yet. Prices start at US$150, through on.com and selected stores. Burna Boy became an On ambassador just over a year ago.
pts: All-red Cloudmonster plus an all-white tennis shoe
From US$150, available now
Cloudtilt Remix still to come

stories.h: SATISFY x adidas second running capsule lands Oct 30
sum: Paris running label SATISFY and adidas are releasing their second Adizero collab: the Adios Pro Evo 2 and an Adios built on the Adios 9, made for track sessions, tempo runs and races up to 10 km. Each comes in an earthy brown or a light blue colorway.

Both have metallic silver Three Stripes, matte gold SATISFY lettering and SATISFY's tagline printed under the heel tab. The tech includes a Lightlock stretch upper, Lightstrike Pro foam and Continental rubber on the forefoot. The limited release lands October 30 on adidas.com. No price has been announced.
pts: Two shoes, each in Earth brown or light Blue
Limited release on October 30 at adidas
Gold lettering and silver stripes

stories.h: Air Max 90 'Light Orewood Brown' goes patent and see-through
stories.why: Easy casual sneaker with a twist
sum: Nike's latest Air Max 90 has a mesh base with translucent overlays on the sidewalls and around the laces, plus glossy beige patent leather mudguards. The tongue labels and heel tab are clear and glassy, and the outsole is semi-translucent. The palette is mostly Light Orewood Brown and sail, with small touches of blue tint and olive.
A metallic Swoosh hangtag carries a pattern that also appears on the printed insoles. It drops November 1 on nike.com for US$145.
pts: Patent mudguards with clear, glassy details
US$145, out November 1
Neutral base with blue and olive hints

stories.h: Matt Hui's SS27 turns childhood uniforms into whimsy
sum: For his second season, Hong Kong designer Matt Hui riffs on clothes from childhood: school uniforms, PE kits, scout gear, workwear and pajamas. Scarves and ties are built into the garments, pinstripes recur, and the tailoring is softened with odd proportions.

He uses cotton lawn, jersey, paper yarn and cashmere, with floral embroidery, pointelle knits and hand-crocheted flower accessories. Everything follows his one-size-fits-all approach. The campaign is shot as a dreamlike game of hide-and-seek, and no stockists or release dates have been announced yet.
pts: School-uniform and PE-kit references
Crocheted flowers and pointelle knits
One-size-fits-all cuts

stories.h: Israel strikes Gaza's Islamic University twice in hours; eight killed across Gaza
sum: Israeli attacks killed at least eight Palestinians across Gaza on Sunday, Al Jazeera reports. Two strikes hit the Islamic University campus in Gaza City within hours: a drone strike wounded seven female students, then an air strike killed three security guards. Other deaths were reported in al-Mawasi near Khan Younis, east of Deir el-Balah and near Hamad Hospital in the north, according to hospitals and the Wafa agency.

Gaza's Health Ministry says at least 1,551 people have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire began, and 74,544 since October 2023. UNESCO estimates nearly 95% of Gaza's higher-education campuses are destroyed or damaged. Israel controls or restricts almost two-thirds of the Strip while food shortages worsen.
pts: Islamic University hit twice in one day; three guards killed, seven students hurt
Health Ministry: 1,551 killed since the 'ceasefire' began
UNESCO: ~95% of Gaza university campuses damaged or destroyed

stories.h: Hebron under lockdown: 2,500 forced out, homes turned into army posts
sum: Israel has sealed off Hebron after a Friday checkpoint shooting that killed two soldiers and two Palestinian suspects. The Palestinian Prisoner's Society says at least 47 people have been detained since; about 2,500 residents have been forced out, homes converted into military posts and dozens of buildings slated for demolition. In Ein Deir Bahha, the municipality says nearly 500 families were uprooted from 350 dunams.

Al Jazeera explains why this matters beyond the city: Hebron produces about 40% of Palestinian industrial output, so closures squeeze the whole West Bank economy. Rights researchers call it an eviction campaign and collective punishment, while Finance Minister Smotrich has moved to seize planning powers over the Ibrahimi Mosque and the H2 zone.
pts: ~2,500 displaced, 47 detained, mass demolitions under way
Hebron is ~40% of Palestinian industry; lockdown hits whole West Bank
Smotrich claims planning power over Ibrahimi Mosque, eroding 1997 deal

stories.h: Amnesty: Israel's election must not distract from its crimes
stories.why: Pressure on Israel ahead of its vote
sum: Ahead of Israel's 27 October parliamentary vote, Amnesty International warns that Palestinians have little reason to expect change. It says candidates have used dehumanising language, pledged to entrench West Bank annexation and threatened more destruction in Gaza, while parties across the spectrum tried to disqualify Balad leader Sami Abu Shehadeh, a Palestinian citizen of Israel.

Amnesty lists ongoing demolitions, settler attacks during the olive harvest, post-ceasefire killings in Gaza and attacks in Lebanon and Syria. It notes millions under Israeli control cannot vote, though settlements get polling stations. It urges an arms embargo, suspension of the EU-Israel Association Agreement and pressure to end what it calls genocide and apartheid.
pts: Israel votes 27 October; Amnesty expects no rights improvement
Bid to disqualify Palestinian Balad leader Abu Shehadeh
Calls for arms embargo and suspending EU-Israel trade deal

stories.h: Google DeepMind engineer quits over military AI and Israel contracts
sum: The Intercept profiles Sofia Liguori, a DeepMind research engineer in London who resigned in protest at Google's military work, including Project Nimbus with Israel and a classified Pentagon AI contract announced in April. She joined to build AI for power grids, then became active with No Tech for Apartheid and helped organise a demonstration outside the London office.

Liguori says internal posts using the word genocide were deleted and HR told her to watch her tone; Google says it reviews contracts consistently and lets staff raise concerns without retaliation. She argues AI targeting dehumanises people and blurs accountability, and that DeepMind's new union should consider striking rather than petitioning.
pts: Resigned over Project Nimbus and Pentagon AI deals
Says posts mentioning genocide were deleted internally
DeepMind staff unionised in May; she urges strike action

stories.h: Two years of Prabowo-Gibran, through women activists' eyes
sum: Konde.co marks the government's second anniversary by interviewing Afifah of Perempuan Mahardhika and NTT rights activist Sarah Lery Mboeik. The piece cites Amnesty International Indonesia's count of at least 406 attacks on human rights defenders and concern that the revised TNI law weakens civilian control. Afifah says wages barely rose while the free-meals programme drew most of its Rp335 trillion budget from education funds.

Mboeik describes gender-blind disaster response after the Flores quake, criminalisation of customary land defenders, militarisation via new army commands, fuel shortages and health-centre downgrades in eastern Indonesia. Both point to arrests after the August 2025 protests and rushed laws, and urge movements to centre eastern Indonesian women and link labour, Indigenous, Papuan and queer struggles.
pts: Amnesty Indonesia: 406+ attacks on rights defenders in two years
MBG budget reportedly 83% from education funds
Calls to decentralise movements away from Jakarta

stories.h: Karo families seek justice after free-meal poisoning
sum: Konde.co follows the family of F, a 16-year-old in Karo, North Sumatra, among 353 students suspected of being poisoned by free nutritious meals (MBG) on 13 August. She developed seizures and memory problems; after five facilities, Jakarta's RSCM attributed symptoms to stress, which the family disputes. Lab tests found Bacillus cereus, Staphylococcus aureus and E. coli in the food, results the family got only after a local DPRD hearing.

The family filed a police report against the school, the local kitchen and the National Nutrition Agency. Monitoring group JPPI counts 43,838 poisoning victims nationwide since 2025, and CELIOS calls for a moratorium. The Constitutional Court has ordered MBG funding separated from the education budget by 2028.
pts: 353 students suspected poisoned in one Karo incident
JPPI: 43,838 MBG poisoning victims since 2025
No clear compensation mechanism in the presidential regulation

stories.h: A year after Padang's flash floods, survivors still waiting
sum: Project Multatuli returns to Batu Busuk, Padang, nearly a year after the November 2025 floods from the Batang Kuranji river destroyed homes, a prayer house and the only paved road. The permanent housing site has only been levelled, the living allowance ended in March, and most farmers lost their fields, turning to hauling driftwood, labour or domestic work. Residents blame upstream land clearing; a geologist also cites steep slopes, extreme rain and climate change.

A geologist says cleanup is far slower than after the 2012 flood. The deputy mayor estimates reconstruction at Rp3.7–3.8 trillion, says the city can't pay and that rivers and bridges are Jakarta's responsibility. Residents remain unclear about a promised Rp1.5 trillion aid package.
pts: Permanent housing not yet built; living allowance stopped in March
Around 60% of residents were farmers, many lost their land
City and central government trade responsibility for rebuilding

stories.h: Aceh Tamiang: palm oil on riverbanks and the post-flood livelihood trap
stories.why: Land, palm oil and disaster risk
sum: Project Multatuli examines palm plantations along Aceh's Tamiang River nearly a year after the late-2025 Sumatra floods. Smallholders describe trees and homes swept away, incomes collapsing and husbands migrating for work; some sell timber before it matures or replant palms on credit. The district has about 24,759 hectares of smallholder palm, and its spatial plan reserves over 8,500 hectares as river buffers.

WALHI Aceh and Sawit Watch say riverbanks shouldn't be replanted with palm, but any transition needs mixed gardens, seedlings and markets so farmers aren't pushed back to palm. The province says it's checking corporate concession permits first. Several agencies didn't respond to questions before publication.
pts: Farm incomes fell sharply after floods destroyed riverside palms
Buffer-zone rules exist but replanting support is slow
Activists: ban palm on banks only with alternative livelihoods

stories.h: Serbia's Vucic concedes defeat to student-led movement
sum: Aleksandar Vucic conceded that his Serbian Progressive Party, in power since 2012, lost Sunday's snap parliamentary election to the Student List. By his own projection the students won 135–140 of 250 seats, against about 105 for his list. The movement grew out of nearly two years of protests after a railway station canopy collapse in Novi Sad killed 16 people in November 2024.

Turnout was the highest since 1992. Watchdog CRTA reported voter pressure at nearly a third of observed polling stations, and CeSID logged about 260 possible irregularities. Crowds celebrated in Belgrade and Novi Sad. Many Student List candidates are doctors and teachers with no political experience.
pts: Student List projected to win a majority of 250 seats
Movement born from Novi Sad canopy collapse protests
Record turnout despite reported voter pressure

stories.h: Lula beats Flavio Bolsonaro in Brazil runoff comeback
sum: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Brazil's presidential runoff with just over 51% against right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, a margin of more than four million votes, after trailing in the first round. He campaigned on cost of living, a shorter workweek and floated free weekend public transport. At 80, he begins a fourth term on 5 January 2027.

Bolsonaro has not conceded, calling the result unacceptable and objecting to a court-backed two-hour voting extension, which both campaigns had requested. Al Jazeera notes Lula faces a right-leaning Congress. Trump-era tariffs and sanctions on Brazilian judges had backed the Bolsonaro family; Sheinbaum and Sanders congratulated Lula.
pts: Lula ~51% to Bolsonaro ~48%
First modern Brazilian to lose round one and win
Bolsonaro refuses to concede, seeks annulment
